## Skills

### AI Strategy

| Skill | Lifecycle | Editions | Reviewers | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ai-strategy:ai-maturity-assessment` | Discover, Improve | starter, scale, enterprise | none | Diagnoses an organisation's current AI maturity across strategy, people and adoption, knowledge, governance, platform and delivery capability, and value measurement, using observed evidence rather than self-scored opinion, and maps the result to a CopilotForge archetype. Use when a programme is starting, when leaders disagree about how ready they are, or when a strategy refresh needs an honest baseline. |
| `ai-strategy:ai-operating-model` | Mobilise, Scale | starter, scale, enterprise | design-authority | Designs the target operating model for AI - who decides, who builds, who supports and who owns value - choosing a central, hub-and-spoke or federated shape to suit the edition and archetype, and placing the Centre of Excellence within it. Use when AI work is spreading without clear ownership, when leaders ask how AI should be organised, or before a CoE is chartered. |
| `ai-strategy:ai-roadmap` | Mobilise, Scale, Improve | starter, scale, enterprise | design-authority | Builds a prioritised, sequenced AI roadmap across the Adopt AI, Build with AI and Scale AI journeys and the lifecycle stages, showing dependencies, capacity, foundations and review points against the agreed outcomes. Use when leaders need a plan for the next twelve to twenty-four months, when initiatives compete for the same people, or when an existing roadmap has drifted from its outcomes. |
| `ai-strategy:ai-vision` | Discover, Envision | starter, scale, enterprise | none | Articulates the organisation's AI ambition - a deliberately chosen level of ambition, a short vision statement staff can repeat, a narrative of how work will change and a handful of guiding principles - agreed by the leadership team and written for the whole workforce. Use when leaders cannot say in a sentence why the organisation is adopting AI, when functions hold competing pictures of it, or before outcomes and a roadmap are set. |
| `ai-strategy:executive-sponsorship` | Envision, Mobilise, Scale | starter, scale, enterprise | none | Secures and equips an active executive sponsor for the whole AI programme - choosing the right executive, agreeing time, decision rights and visible behaviours in a sponsor agreement, building a peer sponsor coalition and checking sponsor engagement each quarter. Use when an AI programme has no sponsor or only a nominal one, when the sponsor has gone quiet, or when the sponsor changes role. |
| `ai-strategy:investment-case` | Envision, Mobilise, Scale | starter, scale, enterprise | none | Builds the funding case for the AI programme as a whole across the Adopt, Build and Scale journeys - investment options, full cost of ownership by category, benefit ranges tied to strategic outcomes, staged funding tranches released at evidence gates and the funding model. Use when leaders must decide how much to invest in AI overall, when a budget round needs a programme request, or when funding was approved for licences alone. |
| `ai-strategy:platform-strategy` | Envision, Mobilise, Scale | starter, scale, enterprise | design-authority, security-privacy | Sets the organisation's strategic position on the Microsoft AI platform mix - Copilot Chat, Microsoft 365 Copilot, agents, Copilot Cowork, Copilot Code, Copilot Studio and Microsoft Foundry - giving each a posture, audience, owner, entry criteria and sequence. Use when leaders ask which Microsoft AI platforms the organisation should offer and to whom, when teams adopt platforms ad hoc, or when Microsoft change prompts a rethink. |
| `ai-strategy:strategic-outcomes` | Envision, Mobilise | starter, scale, enterprise | none | Turns an AI ambition into three to five measurable business outcomes, a short set of AI principles and an explicit statement of where AI will not be used, with clear expectations of the executive sponsor. Use when leaders say they want an AI strategy, when a programme has activity but no agreed outcomes, or when a sponsor needs to explain why the organisation is investing in AI. |
| `ai-strategy:strategy-refresh` | Measure, Improve, Scale | starter, scale, enterprise | none | Refreshes an existing AI strategy on a fixed cycle or a defined trigger, testing the vision, outcomes, platform position and roadmap against measured outcomes, a re-run maturity baseline, Microsoft product change and new regulation, and records what changed and why. Use when the annual strategy review is due, when outcomes are off track, or when a major Microsoft or regulatory change makes the current strategy doubtful. |

### Opportunity Management

| Skill | Lifecycle | Editions | Reviewers | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `opportunity-management:ai-suitability` | Envision, Deliver | starter, scale, enterprise | design-authority | Decides whether a framed business problem should be solved with AI at all, and if so which pattern fits - Copilot Chat, a Cowork task, an agent, Copilot Code, a Foundry solution or plain automation - with the reasoning recorded. Use when an idea arrives at intake, when a team has already picked a tool, or when a sponsor asks why AI is preferable to process change or training. |
| `opportunity-management:backlog-management` | Mobilise, Deliver, Measure | starter, scale, enterprise | none | Sets up and operates the AI opportunity backlog as one visible board - choosing the tool, defining stages with entry and exit rules, mandatory fields per stage, work-in-progress limits, ageing rules, merges, archiving and a regular hygiene routine - so it stays the single route to resources. Use when there is no backlog or several competing lists, when the board is stale or cluttered, or when nobody trusts its status fields. |
| `opportunity-management:business-case` | Envision, Mobilise | starter, scale, enterprise | design-authority, responsible-ai | Writes a proportionate business case for one significant AI initiative - choosing no case, a light case or a full case by cost, risk and reach, then setting out options including a non-AI option, build and run costs, benefits from the value hypothesis, risks, the ask and the decision. Use when a single agent, automation or engineered solution needs funding or approval beyond delegated limits, or when a sponsor asks for a case before committing. |
| `opportunity-management:effort-assessment` | Envision, Mobilise | starter, scale, enterprise | design-authority | Estimates what an AI opportunity will really take - build effort by pattern, the scarce skills and owners it needs, its dependencies on knowledge, data, platforms and reviewers, and the ongoing run cost after release - as ranges with stated confidence. Use when an opportunity needs a feasibility score, when a team says an agent will take a week, or when nobody has asked who will run and pay for a solution after launch. |
| `opportunity-management:idea-capture` | Discover, Envision | starter, scale, enterprise | none | Designs and runs the organisation's open route for staff to submit AI ideas - the submission channels, a short form, acknowledgement and triage timings, duplicate checks, idea campaigns and feedback to every submitter - so ideas reach the backlog instead of side requests. Use when there is no obvious place to send AI ideas, when ideas arrive through managers and chat threads and get lost, or when submissions have dried up. |
| `opportunity-management:opportunity-prioritisation` | Envision, Mobilise, Scale | starter, scale, enterprise | none | Scores and balances a backlog of framed AI opportunities on value, feasibility, risk, readiness of knowledge and ownership, and strategic fit, and shapes a portfolio of quick wins and strategic bets. Admits nothing without an owner, problem, outcome, risk tier and suitability decision. Use when ideas outnumber capacity, when a steering group must choose what goes next, or when the backlog has lost its link to outcomes. |
| `opportunity-management:pilot-selection` | Mobilise, Deliver, Measure | starter, scale, enterprise | evaluation-quality, responsible-ai | Chooses which AI opportunities to pilot and designs each pilot so it can prove or disprove its value hypothesis - a representative cohort, a comparison, a fixed duration, success and stop thresholds set in advance, quality checks, risk containment and an exit plan. Use when an opportunity is ready to test with real users, when pilots keep running indefinitely, or when a pilot ended and nobody could tell whether it worked. |
| `opportunity-management:portfolio-balancing` | Mobilise, Scale, Improve | starter, scale, enterprise | none | Reviews the whole AI opportunity portfolio, planned and in flight, and rebalances its mix across quick wins, strategic bets and foundation work, risk-tier exposure, scarce owner and reviewer capacity, business units, outcomes and platforms, then decides what to start, pause, accelerate or stop. Use when the portfolio feels lopsided, when reviewers or owners are overloaded, or at each quarterly portfolio review. |
| `opportunity-management:problem-framing` | Envision | starter, scale, enterprise | none | Turns a raw idea or tool request into a framed business problem with a named business owner, affected roles, current cost, expected outcome and baseline, and politely sends solution-first requests back to the problem. Use when an idea arrives at intake, when someone asks for an agent or Copilot feature before saying what is wrong, or when a pilot cannot say what it was meant to improve. |
| `opportunity-management:risk-classification` | Envision, Assure, Scale | starter, scale, enterprise | security-privacy, responsible-ai, evaluation-quality, design-authority | Assigns a progressive risk tier from 0 to 4 to an AI opportunity or solution by rating impact, reach, data sensitivity and autonomy, then derives the minimum governance posture and the reviewer gates it must pass, and re-classifies when scope changes. Use when an idea has a chosen pattern, when a solution is about to be shared more widely, or when someone asks which reviews a build needs. |
| `opportunity-management:scale-or-stop` | Measure, Scale, Improve | scale, enterprise | evaluation-quality, security-privacy | Makes the evidence-based decision after a pilot or first release to scale, iterate, pivot or stop, judged against the value hypothesis, adoption, quality and cost, and treats a well-evidenced stop as a success. Use when a pilot reaches its review date, when a sponsor wants to roll a solution out wider, or when a live initiative has been running for months without anyone deciding its future. |
| `opportunity-management:value-hypothesis` | Envision, Mobilise | starter, scale, enterprise | none | States the expected value of a framed AI opportunity as a testable hypothesis before anything is built - the mechanism of change, the measure, its baseline, an expected range, the date it should show, leading indicators and the result that would disprove it. Use when an opportunity is about to be prioritised or piloted, when a team claims an agent will save time without saying how, or when nobody can say what would count as failure. |

### Value Realisation

| Skill | Lifecycle | Editions | Reviewers | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `value-realisation:adoption-to-value-metrics` | Mobilise, Launch, Measure, Improve | starter, scale, enterprise | security-privacy | Builds the measurement chain from adoption to benefit - usage, then scenario behaviour, then work outcome, then benefit - choosing leading indicators for their link to a named benefit and diagnosing where the chain breaks, so usage is never reported as value. Use when reports show active users but no outcomes, when a sponsor treats adoption as return, or when early warning is needed before benefits can be measured. |
| `value-realisation:baseline-design` | Envision, Mobilise, Deliver, Measure | starter, scale, enterprise | security-privacy | Designs the baselines that must be captured before an AI change goes live - exact measure definitions, method, window, data source, sample and a comparison group where fair - so benefits can be proven later rather than asserted. Use when a launch or pilot date is set and nothing has been measured, when baselines rest on memory or vendor figures, or when seasonal or parallel change would make a simple before-and-after misleading. |
| `value-realisation:benefit-hypothesis` | Envision, Mobilise, Deliver | starter, scale, enterprise | none | Turns an approved value hypothesis into formal benefit statements, each with one change, one measure, a direction, a baseline, a target range, timing, an owner role, the enabling changes it depends on and any expected dis-benefits, ready for the benefits register. Use when an opportunity has been approved, when a case lists vague benefits such as efficiency or better insight, or when two solutions claim the same benefit. |
| `value-realisation:benefit-owner` | Mobilise, Deliver, Measure, Improve | starter, scale, enterprise | none | Assigns an accountable business owner role to every benefit, agrees what ownership means - influencing the change, signing off baseline and target, deciding how released capacity is used, reporting and escalating - and sets up the support, hand-over and escalation owners need. Use when benefits sit with IT or the CoE, when an owner has moved role, or when owners have signed up to benefits they cannot influence. |
| `value-realisation:benefit-realisation-plan` | Mobilise, Deliver, Launch, Measure, Improve | starter, scale, enterprise | none | Plans how AI benefits will be realised over time - the benefits register, each benefit's profile by period, the enabling changes and decisions as milestones, measurement points, owners, review cadence, tolerances and closure rules - so value is tracked to closure rather than declared at launch. Use when a case is approved, when benefits have no dates or tracking, or when a portfolio needs one register and review rhythm. |
| `value-realisation:financial-benefits` | Envision, Mobilise, Measure, Improve | starter, scale, enterprise | none | Quantifies the financial benefits of AI work with the finance function, classifying each as cashable, non-cashable, cost avoidance or revenue, agreeing the valuation method, evidence and budget line, and keeping released time apart from cash until a decision redeploys or removes cost. Use when a case or CFO needs money figures, when hours saved are being multiplied into savings, or when benefits must be banked in budgets. |
| `value-realisation:non-financial-benefits` | Envision, Mobilise, Measure, Improve | starter, scale, enterprise | none | Measures AI benefits that should not be forced into money - customer and employee experience, risk and compliance reduction, decision quality, resilience and organisational capability - with defined indicators, baselines, owners and an evidence standard for each, and no spurious cash value. Use when a case rests on experience or risk reduction, when finance dismisses soft benefits, or when capability gains need evidence a sponsor will accept. |
| `value-realisation:post-implementation-review` | Measure, Scale, Improve | starter, scale, enterprise | none | Runs a post-implementation review an agreed period after an AI solution or programme goes live, comparing actual outcomes, costs, adoption, quality and risk with the approved case, explaining each variance, capturing lessons and agreeing actions for benefits still to come. Use when a live solution reaches its review date, when a funding body asks whether the case was delivered, or when lessons should improve how future cases are estimated. |
| `value-realisation:productivity-measurement` | Deliver, Launch, Measure, Improve | starter, scale, enterprise | security-privacy | Measures the productivity effect of Copilot, agents, Cowork tasks and automation credibly - throughput, cycle time and capacity released from work data, sampled timing and comparison groups - and tracks where released capacity went, keeping self-reported hours saved as a perception measure only. Use when an hours-saved survey is challenged, when a sponsor asks what people did with saved time, or when a pilot must show a productivity effect. |
| `value-realisation:quality-measurement` | Deliver, Launch, Measure, Improve | starter, scale, enterprise | evaluation-quality | Measures how AI-assisted work changes business quality after launch - accuracy, rework, errors reaching customers, compliance exceptions and consistency - through sampled review against a rubric, operational defect data and comparison with unassisted work. Use when a sponsor asks whether AI-assisted work is better or only faster, when rework or complaints rise after launch, or when productivity gains need a quality guard. |
| `value-realisation:roi-model` | Envision, Mobilise, Measure, Scale, Improve | starter, scale, enterprise | none | Builds a transparent return-on-investment model for an AI initiative or portfolio - full costs across licences, consumption, build, run, review effort, support and change, benefits by class and timing, low, central and high ranges, sensitivity to key assumptions and an assumptions log. Use when a case or renewal needs a return figure, when an ROI number cannot be traced to its inputs, or when estimated and actual return must be compared. |
| `value-realisation:value-dashboard` | Measure, Scale, Improve | starter, scale, enterprise | security-privacy | Specifies a sponsor value dashboard for the AI portfolio across value, adoption, capability and governance, with each tile's measure, method, confidence, baseline, owner and source, plus the data flow from the benefits register, refresh, access, minimum group size and caveats, ready for a report builder. Use when sponsors need one view of realised value, when a dashboard shows usage alone, or when a chosen scorecard now needs building. |

Use when outputs affect people differently, when a solution serves a diverse audience, or when someone suspects bias. |
| `responsible-ai:human-oversight` | Envision, Deliver, Assure, Launch, Improve | starter, scale, enterprise | responsible-ai | Decides the level of human oversight an AI solution needs - review of every output, approval before action, sampling or monitoring - and reviews whether the reviewers have the time, information, competence and authority to catch and overturn errors, classifying gaps as blocking or advisory. Use when outputs affect people, money or safety, when an agent will act with less supervision, or when human review exists only on paper. |
| `responsible-ai:prohibited-use-review` | Discover, Envision, Assure, Improve | starter, scale, enterprise | responsible-ai | Screens a proposed or live AI use against the organisation's prohibited and restricted uses, Microsoft's acceptable use terms and regulation as advised by legal - covert monitoring of staff, emotion inference, social scoring, manipulation, unreviewed decisions about individuals - and records a stop, restrict or proceed verdict. Use when a sensitive idea arrives at intake, when a solution's purpose drifts, or when asked if a use is allowed. |

| `ai-centre-of-excellence:coe-champion-integration` | Mobilise, Enable, Scale, Improve | starter, scale, enterprise | none | Connects the Champions network to the AI Centre of Excellence - assigning the knowledge, process, adoption and AI Champion roles to CoE pillars, defining what each contributes to intake, knowledge upkeep, testing and stories, what they never approve, and how work and feedback flow both ways. Use when a CoE and a Champions programme run side by side without links, or when Champions have become the CoE's unpaid build team. |
| `ai-centre-of-excellence:coe-charter` | Mobilise, Scale | starter, scale, enterprise | none | Drafts the charter for an AI Centre of Excellence - purpose, who owns what between the business, AI enablement and the sponsor, scope across the six pillars, decision rights, launch commitments and what the CoE is not - or the lighter terms of an AI working group. Use when leadership asks for an AI CoE, when a group has drifted into a reporting forum or request queue, or when a sponsor needs one page to agree before people are appointed. |
| `ai-centre-of-excellence:coe-delivery-model` | Mobilise, Deliver, Assure, Launch, Scale | scale, enterprise | design-authority, evaluation-quality, security-privacy | Defines how the CoE actually builds and releases agents and automations once work is approved - delivery routes from self-service makers to CoE-assisted, CoE-built, partner and pro-code teams, a definition of ready and of done by risk tier, maker support, reusable patterns and handover to operations. Use when approved work has no clear way to get built, when makers and partners work differently, or when solutions go live unsupported. |
| `ai-centre-of-excellence:coe-governance-model` | Mobilise, Assure, Launch, Improve | starter, scale, enterprise | security-privacy, responsible-ai, evaluation-quality, design-authority | Writes a proportionate AI governance framework and acceptable-use starter - five governance areas, progressive risk tiers 0 to 4 with minimum controls, an agent portfolio register with business, knowledge and technical owners, and reviewer gates - so low-risk experimentation is not blocked. Use when there is no approved AI policy, when departments build agents with no register or owner, or when governance is so heavy people work around it. |
| `ai-centre-of-excellence:coe-knowledge-pillar` | Mobilise, Enable, Deliver, Improve | starter, scale, enterprise | none | Runs the CoE's knowledge management pillar - a pillar lead, the layered knowledge asset register, owners and review dates for the content agents rely on, a knowledge check in intake, knowledge champions, and a loop that turns agent failures into content fixes - applying the knowledge-management standards. Use when the pillar exists on paper only, when agents give outdated answers, or when nobody owns the content solutions ground on. |
| `ai-centre-of-excellence:coe-kpi-framework` | Measure, Scale, Improve | starter, scale, enterprise | none | Builds a KPI framework and scorecard for an AI CoE across adoption, capability, portfolio flow, quality, governance and value, each measure with a baseline, target, source and owner, rolled up into a four-quadrant sponsor dashboard at team level. Use when a sponsor asks how they will know AI is working, when reporting relies on licence counts or hours saved, or when steering needs a scorecard before its first value review. |
| `ai-centre-of-excellence:coe-launch-roadmap` | Mobilise, Launch, Deliver, Scale | starter, scale, enterprise | none | Turns an agreed CoE charter and operating model into a dated launch plan across the Establish, Foundation, Deliver and Scale phases - workstreams, milestones, exit criteria, quick-win selection, first-ninety-day actions, dependencies, launch communications and go or hold decisions at each phase boundary. Use when the CoE is approved and needs a plan to start, or when a launch has drifted with no clear next milestone. |
| `ai-centre-of-excellence:coe-maturity-assessment` | Measure, Scale, Improve | scale, enterprise | none | Assesses how mature a running AI Centre of Excellence is across sponsorship, team, opportunity pipeline, knowledge, delivery, governance, adoption and Champions, portfolio and value, using evidence from its own records, and sets the three to five next moves, including whether it is ready for spokes or federation. Use when a CoE has run for six months or more, at its annual review, or when the sponsor asks whether it is working. |
| `ai-centre-of-excellence:coe-operating-model` | Mobilise, Scale, Improve | starter, scale, enterprise | design-authority | Designs how an AI Centre of Excellence runs - a business-owned structure with sponsor, lead, core team, four Champion roles and central AI enablement support, its shape by edition, the collaboration space, the intake-to-delivery flow and a phased launch. Use when a charter is agreed and the CoE now needs people, routes and a workable flow, or when an existing CoE has become a bottleneck. |
| `ai-centre-of-excellence:coe-opportunity-pipeline` | Envision, Mobilise, Deliver, Measure, Improve | starter, scale, enterprise | none | Runs the CoE's opportunity management pillar as a working pipeline - a pillar owner, stages from Identify to Improve with entry and exit criteria, the opportunity-management method used at each stage, triage rhythm, work-in-progress limits, service levels and pipeline health measures. Use when ideas pile up without decisions, when nobody owns the pillar, or when pilots start without passing through assessment. |
| `ai-centre-of-excellence:coe-portfolio-management` | Deliver, Measure, Scale, Improve | scale, enterprise | design-authority | Manages the CoE's whole portfolio of live and planned agents, automations and AI solutions as one view - lifecycle state, owners, tier, value against hypothesis, run cost and review dates - finding duplicates to consolidate, patterns to reuse and solutions to retire, through a quarterly portfolio review. Use when nobody can say what is live or who owns it, when similar agents multiply, or when steering wants to know what the estate delivers. |
| `ai-centre-of-excellence:coe-raci` | Mobilise, Scale, Improve | starter, scale, enterprise | none | Builds a role-based RACI for AI work across the opportunity lifecycle, governance decisions, knowledge ownership, release and value, with exactly one Accountable per activity and the business accountable for outcomes. Use when nobody can say who approves an agent, when IT is being held to account for business benefits, or when a new CoE needs clear responsibilities before its first steering meeting. |
| `ai-centre-of-excellence:coe-readiness` | Discover, Mobilise | starter, scale, enterprise | none | Checks whether an organisation is ready to launch an AI Centre of Excellence - a sponsor who will decide, an owning business unit, a lead with real time, core team capacity, starting demand, knowledge owners, approved-use guidance and enablement support - and returns a launch, launch-with-conditions or not-yet verdict. Use when leadership wants a CoE before anyone has checked the preconditions, or when an earlier CoE attempt stalled. |
| `ai-centre-of-excellence:coe-sponsor-role` | Mobilise, Launch, Improve | starter, scale, enterprise | none | Defines the executive sponsor's role in an AI Centre of Excellence - the decisions only the sponsor takes, time and attendance, a delegate with real authority, visible support for adoption, and what happens when sponsorship fades - and secures the sponsor's written commitment. Use when a CoE needs a sponsor, when the sponsor only receives reports, or when steering keeps deferring decisions upwards. |
| `ai-centre-of-excellence:coe-team-design` | Mobilise, Scale, Improve | starter, scale, enterprise | none | Designs the people side of an AI Centre of Excellence - the lead, pillar leads and core team roles, specialists borrowed from security, data protection, architecture and partners, the skills each role needs, agreed time, sourcing and backfill - and writes the team's terms of reference. Use when the CoE shape is chosen and roles need filling, when the core team is all enthusiasts and no specialists, or when members have no agreed time. |
| `ai-centre-of-excellence:coe-value-tracking` | Measure, Scale, Improve | starter, scale, enterprise | none | Runs the CoE's routine for tracking value delivered - a value ledger with one line per solution showing estimate at intake, baseline, measured result, method and confidence, a monthly update rhythm, roll-up to the sponsor scorecard and the value review, and honest treatment of attribution and unproven claims. Use when steering asks what the CoE has delivered, when value claims vary by teller, or when nobody revisits estimates after release. |

### Organisation Tailoring

| Skill | Lifecycle | Editions | Reviewers | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `organisation-tailoring:ai-profile-intake` | Discover | starter, scale, enterprise | none | Creates or validates an organisation profile - size, business units, regulatory context, Microsoft estate, current AI use, knowledge, governance, adoption and delivery capability - by short interview or from a file, capturing only what tailoring needs and marking unknowns. Use when someone asks for help with an AI programme and no profile exists, when a profile file is supplied, or when circumstances have changed since the last pack. |
| `organisation-tailoring:ai-role-catalogue` | Mobilise, Enable, Scale | starter, scale, enterprise | none | Maintains the catalogue of AI transformation roles - department lead roles plus sponsor, business, knowledge, solution and reviewer roles - each with purpose, responsibilities, decisions, capabilities, separation rules and typical time, and maps them to the job roles the organisation has declared. Use when an operating model names roles nobody recognises, when job titles must be matched to AI roles, or when the catalogue needs updating. |
| `organisation-tailoring:capability-gap-analysis` | Envision, Mobilise, Scale | starter, scale, enterprise | none | Compares what the recommended AI programme demands - capabilities and time by role and quarter - with what the organisation has declared, classifies each shortfall as capability, capacity or vacancy, and chooses how to close it (develop, recruit, partner, borrow, re-sequence or defer) with the effect on the programme. Use when a pack or roadmap looks unstaffable, when capacity is the stated constraint, or before committing to delivery dates. |
| `organisation-tailoring:edition-and-archetype` | Discover, Envision | starter, scale, enterprise | none | Applies the CopilotForge tailoring rules to a validated organisation profile to recommend an edition (starter, scale or enterprise), an assurance overlay and a maturity archetype, citing the rule id behind each, reporting emerging signals and explaining the result to the sponsor before any pack is built. Use when a profile is ready, when a sponsor asks why they got a lighter or heavier programme, or when circumstances change. |
| `organisation-tailoring:operating-model-tailoring` | Envision, Mobilise | starter, scale, enterprise | none | Right-sizes the AI target operating model for one organisation from its confirmed edition, overlay, archetype, signals and declared constraints - which structures to adopt now, which roles to combine, which forums to merge, what a partner covers, what to defer and what would trigger a change - each decision traced to a rule or constraint. Use when a generic operating model looks too heavy or too light, or when constraints change. |
| `organisation-tailoring:ownership-map` | Mobilise | starter, scale, enterprise | none | Produces a role-based ownership map for an AI programme from declared roles only - the accountable role for each engaged department and each pack artefact, named owners only where the organisation has declared them, and roles left without an owner. Use when a transformation pack needs owners, when a sponsor asks who will do this work, or when nobody can say who owns adoption, governance or agents. |
| `organisation-tailoring:transformation-pack-refresh` | Measure, Scale, Improve | starter, scale, enterprise | none | Refreshes an existing transformation pack when the organisation's profile, signals or the CopilotForge library change - compares old and new profiles and tailoring results, classifies each change as material or minor, maps it to affected artefacts, protects decisions already taken, and agrees a change summary before any document is replaced. Use when a pack is due for review, after a merger or new regulation, or when agents or shadow AI appear. |
| `organisation-tailoring:transformation-pack` | Discover, Envision, Mobilise, Enable, Deliver, Assure, Launch, Measure, Scale, Improve | starter, scale, enterprise | security-privacy | Orchestrates a tailored AI transformation pack from a confirmed profile - assessment, target operating model, adoption and Champions programmes, CoE, opportunity process, agent delivery, governance, roadmap, ownership map, templates and success measures - at the depth the edition sets, each artefact naming its responsible skill and sources. Use when an organisation asks for help adopting Copilot, scaling agents or setting up an AI CoE. |

## Programmes

| Programme | Status | Purpose | Artefacts |
|---|---|---|---|
| `adoption` Copilot Adoption | skeleton | Turn licences into consistent, responsible, role-based use with measurable outcomes. | adoption-readiness, scenario-catalogue, adoption-programme, adoption-measures, communications-plan, learning-plan, support-model |
| `agent-factory` Agent Factory | skeleton | Give every agent idea one route from intake to retirement, with knowledge readiness, testing, reviewer gates and an owner. | opportunity-process, ai-suitability, agent-brief, knowledge-readiness, agent-test-plan, agent-release, scale-or-stop, knowledge-readiness-report, evaluation-plan, agent-card, support-and-monitoring |
| `ai-coe` AI Centre of Excellence | skeleton | Establish a business-owned, AI-enabled operating model that governs once and repeats everywhere. | coe-charter, coe-operating-model, coe-raci, coe-cadence, kpi-framework, coe-terms-of-reference, coe-launch-plan |
| `ai-transformation` AI Transformation | skeleton | The superset programme. Orchestrates strategy, adoption, Champions, CoE, delivery, assurance, operations and value realisation into one coherent transformation pack (decision D10). | operating-model, ownership-map, pack-index, programme-charter, benefits-plan |
| `champions` Copilot Champions | skeleton | Build distributed capability through an evidence-led Champion community with clear operating boundaries. | champion-charter, capability-framework, challenge-catalogue, recognition-model, champion-guide |
| `discovery` Microsoft AI Discovery | skeleton | Understand context, ambition, current use and maturity, then agree outcomes and a first roadmap before any product decision. | maturity-assessment, strategic-outcomes, roadmap |
| `governance` AI Governance | skeleton | Put proportionate controls in place, rising with impact, reach, data sensitivity and autonomy. | governance-framework, risk-classification, data-exposure-review, privacy-assessment, solution-inventory, environment-zoning, impact-assessment |
